title: Adaptive microwindow recommender with SLO-aware throttling and staged rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an adaptive microwindow batching recommender (MBR) that suggests per-route microbatch time windows and concurrent throttle targets to reduce token cost while preserving latency SLOs. The recommender combines short-term traffic forecasts, per-route latency profiles, and an anomaly-aware safety layer. Apply flow must be staged: dry-run on shadow traffic, limited canary with circuit breakers, then progressive rollouts with automated rollback on SLO degradations. This ticket implements the core recommender, the safe-apply orchestration, and the anomaly detector used by the rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria: MBR produces per-route microwindow and throttle suggestions with confidence scores for 95% of active routes
Shadow dry-run can execute recommended config on 1000 rps equivalent without affecting production latency
Canary apply respects circuit-breaker rules: automatic rollback when route p99 latency exceeds baseline + 10% for 3 consecutive mins
End-to-end test demonstrates >= 12% median token-cost reduction on synthetic workload while keeping p99 within SLO bounds
Playbook and runbook created and reviewed by SRE and PM with rollback steps and monitoring links
tasks: Design model: define microwindow feature set and forecast model (traffic seasonality, request size distribution, model seq length)
Implement offline recommender prototype (Python) and integrate with metrics export for route sampling
Build online scorer that runs in Console backend and exposes suggestions via API
Implement shadow-dry-run pipeline that mirrors requests and measures hypothetical latency/throughput impact
Create canary orchestration: staged apply, progressive scaling, circuit-breaker and automated rollback hooks
Add anomaly detector: EWMA + quantile drift detector with alerting to PagerDuty
Create dashboards: per-route recommendation, predicted vs observed, rollback triggers
Write runbook and safety checklist; run a staged internal experiment
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes added. Initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/MBR+Adaptive+Microwindow (internal). Goal: reduce per-token cost without manual tuning.

2026-02-22 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype working on sampled routes. Early results show 15% token-cost reduction on low-latency routes but p99 regressions on spiky traffic. Added traffic forecast feature to model to avoid aggressive window increases during ramps.

2026-02-27 - Review (SRE): Suggested adding dual-path fast-pass that bypasses microbatching for any request flagged as latency-critical (header marker). Action: add header-based bypass and ensure auth checks preserved.

2026-03-02 - Design feedback (PM - Priya Shah): Prioritize safe-apply UX: must allow manual hold and instant rollback from Console. Logged feature request for a one-click rollback UI in console-2026.04.
2026-03-04 - Engineering note: Implemented shadow dry-run for 500 rps using Kafka mirror topic. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789 (WIP).
2026-03-08 - Experiment: Ran internal canary on 'chat-summaries' route for 30m. Observed cost -18% and p99 +6ms (within SLO+10%). Canary kept, expanded to 10% traffic slice.

2026-03-09 - Incident learning: On one route with high seq-length variance, recommender suggested large microwindow that caused a transient p99 spike when a large-request batch interleaved. Mitigation: add request-size bucketing and limit inter-bucket batching.
2026-03-10 - QA: Added acceptance tests for circuit-breaker threshold behavior and synthetic traffic profile generator. Next: add anomaly detector tuning and final runbook review with SRE team.
notes: Trade-offs considered: heavier forecasting reduces false positives but increases compute for recommender; decided on hybrid (lightweight seasonal model + kurtosis detector) to keep runtime cost low.
Fallback strategy: immediate revert to previously pinned config on rollback; if previously pinned does not exist, switch to conservative defaults (microwindow=1ms, no batching) to ensure latency.
Security: dry-run and shadow traffic sanitized to remove customer PII before mirroring. Security review flagged in project doc.
Follow-ups: add ML-driven confidence calibration, expand to embedding routes, and surface per-route estimated cost-savings in Console.
